item.title: Identities of thousands of Homeland Security employees and contractors disclosed in massive data breach
item.description: An activist group published a searchable database, exposing the identities and contact information for immigration officers, border agents and undercover investigators, according to documents posted online. DHS said it was “aware of a potential breach” and was “working to address the situation swiftly and effectively.”

item.title: Cornell faculty senate moves ahead with no-confidence vote on administration
item.description: Cornell University’s leaders have been under fire since last month, when a former student filed a civil lawsuit alleging that she was the victim of a gang rape at a fraternity house and the school had failed to enact adequate measures to prevent such an assault. An online vote will now take place starting Thursday, with results expected Nov. 6.

item.title: Trump has a lot to say about men’s looks. Take our quiz to guess whom he considers attractive.
item.description: President Donald Trump returned to the campaign trail this month to stump for Republicans in the midterms, holding rallies every day. And just about as often, he has made impromptu comments about the physical attractiveness of other men.

item.title: Flávio Bolsonaro is granted a visa to enter the U.S. after fleeing Brazil following his election loss
item.description: The defeated presidential candidate left Brazil for the United States on Tuesday, according to three people with knowledge of the matter, in defiance of a judicial order to surrender his passport. He and members of his family have been granted U.S. visas, a senior State Department official said. Bolsonaro is under investigation for his over financial ties to a banker accused of financial misconduct and to a man suspected of money laundering tied to Brazil’s betting industry.

item.title: Grand jury declines to indict former White House aide Cassidy Hutchinson over Jan. 6 testimony
item.description: Hutchinson testified before lawmakers about President Donald Trump’s actions during the Jan. 6, 2021, attack on the U.S. Capitol. The failure of the Justice Department to secure the indictment marks the latest rebuke of its efforts to prosecute one of the president’s political enemies.

item.title: CDC’s deputy director to leave Trump administration after six months on the job
item.description: Jennifer Shuford, an infectious-disease physician who had served as Texas’s health commissioner, was hired in April as part of a new four-person leadership team tapped to run the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention and restore confidence in the agency, Trump officials said at the time. She is expected to leave the agency after next week’s midterm elections, according to two people who spoke on condition of anonymity to discuss a sensitive personnel matter.

item.description: The judge wrote that the Trump administration’s defense of Comey’s firing “flies in the face of nearly two centuries of Supreme Court precedent.” Comey had argued in her federal lawsuit that she was terminated because of her father, James B. Comey, whom President Donald Trump fired as head of the FBI during his first term, and because of her perceived political beliefs.

item.title: Brazilian President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva wins reelection, halting Latin America’s shift to the right
item.description: Lula defeated Sen. Flávio Bolsonaro, the 45-year-old son of imprisoned former president Jair Bolsonaro. With more than 99 percent of ballots counted, Lula had captured 51.75 percent of the vote, electoral authorities reported. He is Brazil’s first presidential candidate to finish second in the first round and win the runoff, and the first elected four times.
